bull.b: Consistent TTM operating cash flow (~$1.25B) and free cash flow (~$1.20B) demonstrate durable cash generation that funds R&D, AI investments and GTM without immediate dependence on external capital. High cash conversion cushions execution risk while losses narrow, supporting reinvestment and optionality.

Strong RPO expansion and NRR >120% reflect sticky subscription economics and upsell within an expanding cloud base. Durable, recurring revenue and robust retention create predictable cash flows and support sustained revenue growth even as large migrations proceed, enabling margin leverage over time.

Rapid Rovo adoption is driving materially higher expansion within customers, with users on Rovo growing ARR about twice as fast. Structured AI adoption increases product stickiness, drives higher per-customer monetization and accelerates platform-led growth, improving long-term unit economics and upsell potential.

bear.b: Despite solid cash generation, the company remains GAAP unprofitable with a TTM net margin of -3.5% and ROE around -13%, indicating accounting losses persist. Continued GAAP deficits can constrain investor returns, limit buyback/dividend optionality and pressure profitability-focused stakeholders over the medium term.

Meaningful leverage relative to a volatile equity base raises financial risk: higher interest obligations and reduced flexibility for sizable M&A or capital returns. If growth or FCF weakens, servicing debt could limit strategic options and increase vulnerability to macro stress over a multi-quarter horizon.

Large customer migrations are multi-year and highly customized, slowing seat expansion and creating revenue timing lumpiness. The structural complexity of moving enterprise workloads limits near-term cloud unit growth, complicates sales cycles and can depress marginal expansion rates for sizable installed cohorts.
